title: What rule does the Y-shaped number machine follow?
description: A machine takes two inputs and gives one result. A rule is tried on every pair, written as a formula in the letter-numbers a and b, and then used on a new pair.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rule is trusted only after it matches every pair of inputs and results. Watch for students who trust a rule after one pair matches.

source: A Y-shaped number machine gives these results: inputs 5 and
video_script.why: A learner sees that a rule for a machine is trusted only when it matches every pair.
video_script.substitution: the book's Y-shaped machine with four pairs of inputs and results, and the new inputs six and four
video_script.anchor: the Y-shaped number machine of the book with two inputs and one result
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says one matching pair is enough to trust a rule. The rule must match every pair, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The formula is two eigh minus b, and the inputs six and four give eight.

final_answer.spoken: two eigh minus b, and the inputs six and four give eight

maths_rules: rule: two times the first input minus the second
first input a, second input b: formula 2a - b
Keeko test: sum plus one matches 5 and 2 (8) but gives 10 for 8 and 1, not 15
video_script.design: The machine stays on the board; one rule is tried on each pair in turn, written with letter-numbers, and then used on a new pair.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a Y-shaped machine with two inputs and one result; pairs 5, 2 to 8; 8, 1 to 15; 9, 11 to 7; 10, 10 to 10

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the Y-shaped machine is drawn
marks.pairs: the four pairs of inputs and results appear beside the machine
marks.ask: a question mark appears on the machine

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a puzzle from your book. The Y-shaped machine takes two inputs, and gives one result.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Five and two give eight, and eight and one give fifteen. Nine and eleven give seven, and ten and ten give ten.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What rule does the machine follow?

beats.on_screen: the machine and the four pairs stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one rule for every pair; first input a, second input b; trust a rule only when it matches every pair

marks.rule: one rule is shown acting on every pair
marks.names: the first input is labelled a and the second input is labelled b

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The machine follows one rule for every pair of inputs.
<bookmark mark='names'/>We call the first input eigh, and the second input b.
<bookmark mark='trust'/>We trust a rule only when it matches every pair.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four pairs of inputs with their results.

beats.on_screen: To find: the rule as a formula in a and b, and the result for the inputs 6 and 4

marks.find: the words formula and inputs 6 and 4 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the rule as a formula, and use it on six and four.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: try the rule two times the first input, minus the second

marks.try: the rule 2 × first − second is written beside the machine

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Step one, try a rule. Take two times the first input, then take away the second.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, test the first pair. Two times five is ten, and ten minus two is eight, which matches.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Test the second pair. Two times eight is sixteen, and sixteen minus one is fifteen, which matches.

marks.letters: first input becomes a, second input becomes b, and 2a − b is written

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the third pair. Two times nine is eighteen, and eighteen minus eleven is seven, which matches.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The last pair has two times ten as twenty, and twenty minus ten is ten, which matches.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>The rule fits all four pairs. With eigh and b for the inputs, the rule is two eigh minus b.
<bookmark mark='new'/>Step four, use the rule on six and four. Two times six is twelve, and twelve minus four is eight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 2a − b; the inputs 6 and 4 give 8
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The formula is two eigh minus b, and the inputs six and four give eight.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the machine
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the rule sum plus one, struck out; (5, 2) gives 8 but (8, 1) gives 10, not 15

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the rule sum plus one
marks.test: the pairs (5, 2) and (8, 1) are tried in the bubble
marks.gap: 8 matches, but 10 and 15 do not match

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one matching pair is enough. Five plus two plus one is eight, so Keeko trusts that rule.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try the second pair with the same rule.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Eight plus one plus one is ten, but the machine gave fifteen.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>One match is not enough. The rule must match every pair.
